title: A global view of human centromere variation and evolution.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Figshare API listing (CC BY 4.0, 6 zips: HGSVC3 sequences 900 MB, HGSVC3 annotation 112 MB, HPRC sequences 2.39 GB, HPRC annotation 288 MB, pedigree sequences 215 MB, pedigree annotation 19.5 MB). Downloaded the pedigree annotation zip in full, and pulled three members of the HGSVC3 annotation zip by ranged requests (reading the zip index). HGSVC3 centromeric-region BED has 2,156 contigs = 2,110 HGSVC3 + 23 CHM13 + 23 CHM1, from 65 individuals; CDR (centromere dip region, the hypomethylated kinetochore site) BED has 9,740 raw fragments on all 2,156 contigs; active-array BED has 2,734 rows. Every CDR midpoint falls inside its active array. A per-chromosome mean of relative CDR position leaves a within-chromosome SD (standard deviation) of 0.20, against 0.27 overall. Pedigree set: 483 centromeres, 20 samples, 2,082 CDR fragments. No pedigree individual appears in HGSVC3 (NA12878 absent); three HGSVC3 trios are present.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That CDRs were called with CDR-Finder from ONT (Oxford Nanopore) native-read CpG methylation and validated by CENP-A DiMeLo-seq/CUT&RUN on about 10% of cell lines; the ~6% di-kinetochore and <1% tri-kinetochore rates; the 226 haplotypes and 1,870 HOR (higher-order repeat) variants; mutation rates. I did not open the sequence FASTA zips (over the 50 MB cap) or the per-chromosome HOR annotation BEDs for HGSVC3, beyond the pedigree example (203,155 rows for chr1).

a1_downloadable.note: Public Figshare record, CC BY 4.0, no login; ranged downloads worked (checked).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Kinetochore site is given directly as CDR intervals per centromere contig (checked). Light construction only: merging adjacent CDR-Finder fragments (median 35.7 kb) into sites and labelling windows by interval overlap. The merge gap decides di-kinetochore counts and must be tuned to match the paper's ~6%.

a3_inputs_present.note: Centromere sequences are FASTA in the same record (900 MB zip, not opened). HOR monomer annotation and 5-kb sequence-identity BEDs are in the annotation zip (checked in the pedigree set). No accession lookups needed.

a4_units_stated.note: BED coordinates in base pairs on named contigs (standard convention); the sequence-identity column is percent identity. No header rows, but the formats are standard.

a5_enough_rows.note: 2,156 centromeres with CDR labels (checked), plus 483 pedigree centromeres; window-level examples number in the hundreds of thousands. The independent units are 67 genomes × 24 chromosomes.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~1 GB (annotation BEDs + sequence-identity BED uncompressed ~0.5–0.8 GB; FASTA ~2–3 GB uncompressed only if using raw sequence)
a6_fits_laptop.note: HOR-feature models run on CPU. DNA language-model embeddings need window subsampling.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: 2,156 − 46 CHM13/CHM1 contigs = 2,110, exactly the paper's count; 65 HGSVC individuals plus CHM13 and CHM1 (checked).

a8_label_provenance.note: The label is an algorithmic call (CDR-Finder) on measured ONT methylation, validated against CENP-A profiling on about 10% of lines. Features would be sequence and HOR structure, not methylation, so it isn't circular. Caveat: the methylation calls themselves come from a basecalling neural network.

B1.why: Three BEDs plus per-chromosome HOR BEDs join cleanly on the contig name (checked).

B2.why: Headerless BED files parsed first try with pandas (checked).

B3.why: One pipeline (CenMAP/CDR-Finder) for all 2,156 centromeres; same assay throughout (paper).

B4.why: No censoring, but CDRs come fragmented (9,740 pieces); a merge rule is needed (checked).

B5.why: No duplicate contigs seen. Trio haplotypes are related, which is a split issue, not duplicated rows.

B6.why: Figshare gives a one-paragraph description only; column meanings inferred from BED convention.

C1.why: Either sequence predicts the kinetochore site across individuals, or it's epigenetically free; both outcomes are informative.

C2.why: Searches found no model predicting kinetochore/CDR position from centromere sequence; CDR-Finder is the labeller, not a predictor.

C3.why: Novel: first public, population-scale kinetochore-site labels (2,110 centromeres); likely never modelled.

C4.why: Needs native ONT long reads plus a complete assembly; HiFi-only assemblies (e.g. HPRC) lack CDRs here.

C5.why: Obvious dummy: per-chromosome mean relative position (within-chromosome SD 0.20, computed by me).

D1.why: DNABERT-2 and HyenaDNA are open-weight DNA models with downloadable weights.

D2.why: Freeze-and-head works, but megabase centromeres force window subsampling on CPU; satellites are poorly represented in pretraining.

D3.why: DNABERT-2 is Apache-2.0; data is CC BY 4.0 (checked on Figshare).

E1.why: Hold out whole individuals/trios, or whole chromosomes; sample IDs are in contig names (checked).

E3.why: Per-chromosome mean relative CDR position computed directly from the files.

E4.why: Pedigree transmissions of identical haplotypes show how much the CDR moves with sequence fixed (paper).

E5.why: Paper reports kinetochore position tied to sequence/structure; the CDR must fall inside the active array (verified for all 2,156).

E6.why: Shuffle CDR labels across same-chromosome centromeres; ablate sequence-identity versus HOR features.

E7.why: 483 Platinum pedigree centromeres with CDRs, from individuals not in HGSVC3 (checked).

E8.why: Paper reports associations, not a predictive accuracy to reproduce.

G1.why: Only per-assembly contig coordinates; mapping to CHM13 coordinates needs alignment.

G2.why: HPRC's 5,747 centromeres (same Figshare record, no CDR annotation) are the obvious application set.

G3.why: Contig name joins CDR, array and HOR files one-to-one or cleanly one-to-many.

G4.why: Predicted kinetochores on 5,747 HPRC centromeres could test 'kinetochore mutates fastest' at scale, but only if accurate.

H1.why: Non-kinetochore windows are the negatives, present in every centromere.

H2.why: 28 populations, but all cell lines (mostly lymphoblastoid), one lab pipeline.

H3.why: Claim written below, limited to cell-line methylation dips in complete assemblies.

H4.why: Cell-line origin and the validated subset are stated; the CDR fragmentation rule isn't obvious.

I1.why: Logsdon lab (authors), T2T and HPRC centromere groups annotating HiFi-only assemblies.

I2.why: Could replace ONT methylation calls for locating kinetochores; marginal if ONT is already run.

I3.why: Overlap or distance-to-true-CDR roughly matches a 'where is the kinetochore' decision.

I4.why: Unknown whether a simple 'most homogeneous HOR subregion' rule already does as well.

J1.why: Grouped splits, a sequence backbone and a transfer test to the pedigree set.

J2.why: Needs centromere-biology intuition; the paper's figures give sanity checks.

J3.why: A per-chromosome baseline plus a feature-importance result is shareable on its own.

J4.why: Roughly 3 weeks is plausible but not committed.

J5.why: Kill condition proposed below, not yet written in NOTES.md.

backbone.name: DNABERT-2 (DNA language model), frozen; HyenaDNA as a long-context alternative
backbone.hardware: CPU laptop with subsampled 5-kb windows; a GPU would allow full coverage

integration.partner_dataset: HPRC centromeres (5,747, sequences and HOR annotation in the same Figshare record, no CDRs)
integration.join_key: chromosome and HOR array structure (no shared coordinates; apply the model per contig)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: If sequence predicts kinetochore position, does the predicted kinetochore site carry the elevated mutation rate across 5,747 more centromeres that lack methylation data?

controls.positive_control: The CDR must fall inside the active HOR array (true for all 2,156, checked), and the model should rediscover the paper's link between kinetochore position and local HOR structure/sequence identity.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle CDR positions among same-chromosome centromeres; performance must fall to the per-chromosome mean baseline.
controls.external_validation: 483 Platinum pedigree (CEPH 1463) centromeres with CDRs, from individuals absent from HGSVC3.

honest_claim_h3: Given the sequence and HOR structure of a complete centromere assembly, the model predicts where a lymphoblastoid-cell-line methylation dip (CDR) sits, for genomes unrelated to those in training.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the DNA sequence and repeat structure of a complete human centromere to predict where the kinetochore attaches.
plain_idea.train_on: 2,110 fully assembled human centromeres from 65 people (2,156 including two reference genomes), each with repeat-unit annotations and 5-kb sequence-identity tracks, cut into windows.
plain_idea.predict: Whether each window lies in the kinetochore site. The true answer is the low-DNA-methylation dip measured on native nanopore reads and called by the CDR-Finder tool, partly confirmed by CENP-A (kinetochore histone) profiling.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Centromere groups could locate kinetochores in thousands of assemblies made without methylation data, such as HPRC's. A failure would show kinetochore position is largely epigenetic, not set by sequence.

label_elsewhere.sources: CDR calls also exist for the 483 Platinum pedigree centromeres (same record, checked) and for T2T CHM13/CHM1 (included). CDR-Finder has been applied to other T2T assemblies, but I found no large public CDR table.
label_elsewhere.why: The pedigree set gives an independent held-out test; beyond that, labels are scarce, which is why a sequence predictor would be useful.

risks: Trios (e.g. HG00512/513/514, HG00731/732/733, NA19238/39/40) share centromere haplotypes, so a child's centromere is nearly a copy of a parent's.
The 226 centromere haplotypes mean unrelated people can carry near-identical arrays; random splits would test memorisation.
Overlapping or adjacent windows from the same centromere split across train and test leak position.
Absolute position within a contig depends on how the contig was cut; use position relative to the active array.
leakage_plan.split: Hold out whole individuals with trios grouped (sample ID is the contig-name prefix, seen in files); add a stricter haplotype-cluster holdout by clustering arrays per chromosome on HOR composition; external test on the Platinum pedigree set.
checks: Shuffle CDR labels among same-chromosome centromeres and confirm a collapse to the per-chromosome mean baseline.
Report accuracy against the nearest-training-haplotype similarity; good scores only on near-copies mean memorisation.
Compare with a one-feature rule (highest sequence-identity window) to see whether the model adds anything.
leakage_plan.verdict: Manageable: the leakage comes from shared haplotypes and needs a cluster-level holdout, not just a by-person split.

success_criteria.metric: Median distance (kb) between the predicted and true CDR centre on held-out individuals, plus the fraction of centromeres whose top predicted window overlaps the true CDR; this matches 'where should I look for the kinetochore'.
success_criteria.baselines: Per-chromosome mean relative position (within-chromosome SD 0.20 of array length, computed by me); a single-feature rule using the highest sequence-identity window; no published predictive number exists.
success_criteria.success: Top-window overlap with the true CDR on held-out haplotype clusters clearly above both baselines (e.g. ≥15 percentage points better than the per-chromosome mean), and replicating on the pedigree set.
success_criteria.kill: Stop if, after one week, the model is no better than the single-feature sequence-identity rule on held-out haplotype clusters.

ambitious.why: Publishes centromere/T2T methods; it would take accurate sequence-only kinetochore prediction that transfers to the pedigree set and is applied to HPRC.

realistic.why: Fits a focused analysis of how much sequence determines kinetochore position, with an honest grouped evaluation.

fallback.why: Takes a benchmark or negative result showing that kinetochore position is weakly sequence-determined beyond chromosome identity.

pitch.headline: 2,110 complete human centromeres from 65 people, each with a measured kinetochore site, openly licensed CC BY 4.0, apparently never modelled.
pitch.what_makes_the_data_unusual: Population-scale, base-pair kinetochore labels: 9,740 CDR fragments on 2,156 contigs, plus 483 pedigree centromeres from separate people for external testing (all checked in the files).
pitch.the_win: Locating the kinetochore from sequence on held-out haplotypes, beating the per-chromosome mean (SD 0.20 of array length), and replicating on the pedigree set.
pitch.even_if_it_fails: A grouped-split estimate of how much of kinetochore position is set by sequence versus epigenetics, a question the paper raises with its 'arms race' model.
pitch.who_wants_it: The Logsdon lab and T2T/HPRC centromere groups, deciding whether HiFi-only assemblies need nanopore methylation runs to locate kinetochores.

ml_idea: Window each active HOR array (5 kb), with features from HOR-variant composition, sequence identity and frozen DNABERT-2 embeddings of subsampled windows. Train a per-window classifier for CDR overlap, holding out individuals and haplotype clusters, and test transfer to the Platinum pedigree centromeres.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: about 100k sampled 5-kb windows at roughly 7 windows/s for DNABERT-2 on CPU; gradient boosting on HOR features takes minutes.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Merge CDR fragments, then test whether 'the highest sequence-identity 5-kb window in the active array' already hits the CDR in most held-out centromeres. If so, the project is a one-page note.

verdict_reason: Clean, open, population-scale kinetochore labels with no prior sequence model found. First check whether a one-feature sequence-identity rule already locates the CDR, and settle the fragment-merge rule against the paper's ~6% di-kinetochore rate.
